name: The Rosalind Theatre
blurbs: The house is full, the critics are in, and one member of the company will not take a bow.
A new play, an old rivalry and a door that should have stayed locked.
Everyone in the company knows their lines. Somebody also knew their cue.
Applause, encores and a final scene that was never in the script.
The leading lady is furious, the director is drunk, and the understudy has never looked happier.
Three acts, two intervals and one death that the audience mistook for the play.
Backstage, everyone has a motive. Out front, the audience is still applauding.
A revival of an old melodrama, and a cast with a history nobody wants revived.
It is the last night of the run, and somebody has decided the company is one too large.
The prompter has gone quiet, the stalls are restless, and the second act is running very long.
Everyone said the play was cursed. One of them is about to make sure of it.
A star returns to the theatre that made them. Not everyone is pleased to see them back.
motives: the leading role had been promised to two people
a cruel review had ended a career, and its author had a long memory
the script had been stolen, and the real author was in the building
a forty-year-old understudy had finally run out of patience
the theatre was about to be sold and pulled down
the playwright's name on the poster belonged to somebody else's work
a contract signed years ago still owned every line anyone spoke
the understudy's letters had been going missing for months
a prop gun had once been loaded by mistake, or so the inquest was told
the company's takings had been leaving by the back door for years
a long-lost child had joined the chorus under another name
the critic's next notice would close the show for good
a rival had paid to have the lights fail on opening night
the star's famous voice had been someone else's all along
an old love letter had been used as a prop, and someone in the stalls had recognised the hand
epilogues: {murderer} and {victim} were by themselves in the {area} during the second act. Only one of them made the curtain call, because {motive}.
While the house applauded, {murderer} slipped into the {area} and found {victim}. The motive was hiding in plain sight: {motive}.
The {area} held two people when the lights went down. {murderer} had rehearsed the scene for years: {motive}.
The house roared at the comedy out front. In the {area}, {murderer} finished the real drama with {victim}, because {motive}.
No one misses anyone backstage until their cue. {victim} missed theirs in the {area}, and {murderer} had made sure of it: {motive}.
{murderer} has played many parts, but never better than in the {area} that night. The reason was no act: {motive}.
When the curtain fell, {victim} stayed in the {area} and {murderer} went out to take a bow. It had been a long time coming: {motive}.
{murderer} knew exactly how long the interval would last, and how quiet the {area} would be: {motive}.
